requirement:
During report conversion, on a terminal enabled under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST
display updating progress with elapsed time and completed and total
test-attempt counts. The total MUST count the recorded attempts selected for
conversion. An attempt MUST advance the completed count only after its
conversion has finished or reported a collection failure, including processing
its associated child-process profiles. These counts MUST measure conversion
work regardless of the attempt's test outcome.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress` states only observable behavior. During report conversion on a terminal enabled under `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, it requires the following:
- An updating display shows elapsed time and completed and total test-attempt counts.
- The total counts the recorded attempts selected for conversion.
- The completed count advances only after an attempt's conversion finishes or reports a collection failure, including its child-process profiles.
- The counts measure conversion work whatever the test outcome.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. I checked each clause for a behavior-preserving alternative that would violate it, and found none. Any alternative still has to show the same progress output. For example, the counter could be an atomic, a channel message or a plain loop variable. The progress renderer could be a hand-written one or one from a crate. The completed count could be updated at a different place in the code, so long as it only advances after conversion has finished. None of these choices changes the observable behavior, so none is a structural obligation.

The cited `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal` supplies context only: when progress is shown, the clearing rules and the exit-status rules. That text is also behavioral. There are no implementation roots and no acknowledgments, and none are needed. Whether the behavior is tested is left to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests adequately cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress`. Terminal enablement, no-color behavior and clearing belong to `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, which is cited context and not reassessed here.

- **Updating display with elapsed time and completed/total counts.** `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared]` builds a conversion display with totals 0 and 2. It calls `completed()` and asserts the bar position and the rendered `{n}/{total} attempts` text. It also asserts the elapsed-time marker `[00:00:`. `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy]` checks the same end to end on a real PTY. There the xterm run shows `Converting coverage`, `1/1 attempts` and `[00:`, and the dumb-terminal and redirected runs show none of it.
- **Total counts the recorded attempts selected for conversion.** Per `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#fn[finish]`, the total is the attempts of the current run whose outcome is not pending. The PTY test runs against a store that already holds earlier runs and still sees `1/1 attempts` for a filter that selects one test. A total that included earlier runs' attempts or all fixture tests would therefore fail. The unit test also checks that the total is rendered (totals 0 and 2).
- **Completed advances only after conversion finishes or reports a collection failure.** `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parallel_conversion_is_bounded_and_retains_every_result_in_order]` has the progress callback assert that the attempt's `finished` flag is already set. It makes index 3 return an error and asserts `completed == total`, so a failed conversion also advances the count. The PTY test's `test(missing_profile)` case exercises a real collection failure and still reaches `1/1 attempts` before clearing.
- **Child-process profiles are processed before the count advances.** The PTY test's `test(child_process)` case converts an attempt with two processes and shows `1/1 attempts`. The attempt is recorded with both processes and its profiles are present.
- **Counts measure work regardless of test outcome.** The PTY test covers a successful attempt, a failed attempt (`test(deliberate_failure)`, exit status failure) and a missing-profile attempt. Each shows the `1/1 attempts` count and the clear sequence.

text: During report conversion, on a terminal enabled under
display updating progress with elapsed time and completed and total
test-attempt counts. The total MUST count the recorded attempts selected for
conversion. An attempt MUST advance the completed count only after its
conversion has finished or reported a collection failure, including processing
its associated child-process profiles. These counts MUST measure conversion
work regardless of the attempt's test outcome.
Habeas coverage progress MUST be displayed when stderr is an interactive
terminal and `TERM` is not `dumb`. `NO_COLOR` MUST disable color without
disabling progress. When stderr is redirected or `TERM=dumb`, Habeas coverage
progress MUST NOT emit animation or terminal control sequences.
Temporary progress displays MUST be cleared when their stage ends, including
empty work and early collection failures. Final diagnostics and the coverage
artifact location MUST remain readable. Progress reporting MUST NOT change
coverage results, retained profiles, or command exit status.
